name: Amazon

header.one_liner: AWS is growing 39% again and retail margins are at a record; $220B of capex has turned free cash flow negative.
header.thesis: Amazon earned a record 13.9% operating margin in the September quarter as AWS grew 39% and North America retail margins nearly doubled. The price is capital: 2026 cash capex of about $220B, $60B of investments in OpenAI and Anthropic, and trailing free cash flow of -$42B. Reported earnings also swing with gains on those stakes, so we value Amazon on operating income.

base.eps_label: FY2026E EPS excluding investment gains and losses: operating income (nine months actual plus Q4 guide midpoint $31B) less net interest, taxed at 20%, on 10.93B diluted shares
base.rev_label: FY2026E net sales ($B): nine months $584.1B plus Q4 guide midpoint $243.5B

rev_cagr.why: AWS grew 39% to a $184B run rate and management projects AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. Retail grew mid single digits in the quarter, about 4 points lower because Prime Day moved into Q2. With AWS near a quarter of sales, the base case assumes about 14% total growth.
rev_cagr.source: Amazon Q3 2026 release (segments, CEO statement, Q4 guidance)

margin_end.why: Net margin on operating earnings is about 10.6% this year. AWS earns about 39% operating margin and retail margins are rising, but depreciation from about $220B of 2026 capex is still ahead. The base case lifts net margin two points over three years.
margin_end.source: Q3 2026 release (segment operating income); 10-Q (2026 capex expectation)

share_chg.why: Amazon does not buy back stock in size; diluted shares rose about 0.8% over the past year from stock compensation.
share_chg.source: Diluted share counts, Q3 2025 to Q3 2026

exit_pe.why: Today's multiple is about 31x 2026 operating EPS and 23x consensus 2027. The base case assumes a modest de-rating as heavy capex keeps free cash flow low.
exit_pe.source: Engine judgment; current multiple computed from price and FY26E operating EPS

pillars.title: AWS re-accelerated
pillars.claim: AWS sales grew 39% to $46.0B at a 39% operating margin, its fastest growth in nearly five years.

evidence.t: AWS segment sales $46.0B, +39%; operating income $17.8B vs $11.4B
CEO projects AWS revenue growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028

pillars.test: Does AWS growth stay above 35% as capacity comes online?

pillars.title: Retail margins at a record
pillars.claim: North America operating income rose to $8.7B from $4.8B on 6% sales growth.

evidence.t: North America sales $112.9B, +6%; operating margin about 7.7%
Q4 guide: sales $240B to $247B, operating income $28.5B to $33.5B

pillars.test: Does North America margin hold above 7% through the holiday quarter?

pillars.title: Capex has overwhelmed cash flow
pillars.claim: Trailing free cash flow was an outflow of $42.4B after a $94.8B rise in capex; 2026 cash capex is expected near $220B.

evidence.t: Operating cash flow $168.3B trailing twelve months, +29%
Purchases of property and equipment, net $210.7B in nine months vs $115.9B

pillars.title: Big bets on AI labs
pillars.claim: Amazon invested $50.0B in OpenAI preferred stock and $10.0B in Anthropic in 2026; gains on these stakes swing reported profit.
pillars.test: Value on operating income, not net income.

variant.street: The market pays about 23x consensus 2027 EPS for AWS re-acceleration and rising retail margins.
variant.ours: Operations are the best they have been, but the cash is going into capex and AI stakes. Our base case earns a little above Amazon's cost of equity: a good business at a reasonable price, not yet a bargain.
variant.could_be_wrong: If AWS grows above 40% for two years as management projects and capex then levels off, free cash flow could swing by more than $100B and the stock is cheap.
variant.would_change_mind: AWS growth below 30%, or 2027 capex guided materially above 2026 without faster AWS growth.

moat.summary: Logistics scale, Prime, AWS's customer base and a fast-growing advertising business.
moat.detail: Rated from the latest 10-K and 10-Q; see the moat window for the sources of advantage.

quality.leverage_note: Net debt about $66B (debt about $180B including new notes, against $114B of cash and securities), rising to fund capex and AI investments.
checks: Reported 2026 earnings include large gains on Anthropic and other equity stakes

review.basis: Q3 2026 10-Q and release (quarter to 30 September 2026). Q4 reports in early February; this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: Record margins and AWS back near 40% growth. The catch is capex: free cash flow has gone negative.
review.model: Amazon runs the largest online store, a marketplace for third-party sellers, a fast-growing advertising business and AWS, the largest cloud provider. Retail is high-volume and low-margin; AWS and advertising make most of the profit.

how_it_earns.v: Its own retail sales. Low margin, huge volume.
Commissions and fulfilment fees from marketplace sellers.
Sponsored products and Prime Video ads. High margin.
Cloud computing and AI infrastructure. Most of the operating profit.

mix.note: Reported segments. Operating margin is segment operating income over sales.

rows.label: North America
rows.driver: Retail, marketplace and ads; +6% with Prime Day in Q2

callout.label: Advertising
callout.text: Cuts across the retail segments. $19.6B in the quarter, guided to grow in the high teens in Q4.

review.position: The largest cloud provider and US online retailer. AWS is gaining speed again against Microsoft and Google.

moat.threat: The capex race in AI could lower cloud returns; regulators target marketplace practices.

what_numbers_say.d: $46.0B at a 39% operating margin; $184B run rate.
13.9% overall; North America operating income $8.7B vs $4.8B.
Trailing twelve months, after a $94.8B rise in capex.
$50.0B in OpenAI and $10.0B in Anthropic in 2026.

balance.read: Strong credit, but borrowing to fund capex: net debt about $66B and rising.
facts: Debt about $180B vs cash and securities about $114B
Interest expense $1.7B in Q3 vs $0.5B a year earlier

flags.evidence: Nine-month other income $68.4B, mostly equity revaluations. Q3 net income fell despite operating income up 61%.
Trailing free cash flow -$42.4B vs +$14.8B a year earlier.
Guidance assumes no impact from energy derivative contract remeasurements, a new swing factor in operating income.

forecast_basis.rev_cagr: Driver-based: AWS near 40%, retail mid-to-high single digits
forecast_basis.margin_end: Judgment: mix shift to AWS and ads, offset by depreciation
forecast_basis.exit_pe: Judgment: modest de-rating while free cash flow is low

base.story: AWS grows 30% to 40%, retail margins keep improving, depreciation absorbs part of the gain.

downside.story: AI demand slows while capex keeps rising; AWS margins compress and the multiple falls toward 20x.

upside.story: AWS above 40% for two years and capex peaks; free cash flow swings sharply positive.

risks.how: About $220B of 2026 capex becomes depreciation; if AI prices fall, AWS margins compress.
Growth depends on capacity coming online and a few very large AI customers.
Retail and advertising depend on US consumer spending.
$60B invested in OpenAI and Anthropic this year; write-downs would hit reported earnings.
The FTC case on marketplace practices and EU rules could limit how Amazon ranks and charges sellers.

peer_read.why_premium: AWS is growing faster than at any time in five years and retail margins are at a record; Amazon trades at a discount to Walmart.
peer_read.why_not: Free cash flow is negative and Microsoft offers similar cloud growth with net cash.
peer_read.peers_note: Walmart is valued as a retailer; Microsoft and Alphabet as cloud and software platforms. Amazon is both.

questions: How much of AWS growth comes from a few AI labs that Amazon also invests in?
Should reported earnings or operating earnings drive the valuation?

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Sales grew 12% in the September quarter, about 16% excluding the Prime Day shift. AWS grew 39% and management projects over 40% in 2027 and 2028.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: Logistics scale, Prime and the largest cloud customer base. The risk is a capex race that lowers cloud returns for everyone.

arguments.label: Profitability
arguments.text: Operating margin hit a record 13.9%: AWS earned 39% and North America operating income nearly doubled.

arguments.label: Capital
arguments.text: About $220B of 2026 capex and $60B of AI-lab investments turned trailing free cash flow to -$42B, funded partly with new debt.

arguments.text: {peer_line} Valued on operating earnings, because gains on AI stakes inflate reported EPS.

thesis_long: Amazon's operations have never been stronger. AWS grew 39% in the quarter, its fastest in nearly five years, at a 39% operating margin, and management projects more than 40% growth in both 2027 and 2028. In retail, North America operating income rose to $8.7B from $4.8B and the company posted a record 13.9% operating margin.

The question is capital. Cash capex of about $220B this year, plus $50B invested in OpenAI and $10B in Anthropic, turned trailing free cash flow to -$42B, and interest expense has tripled. Reported earnings are inflated by gains on those AI stakes, so we value Amazon on operating income: about $8 a share this year.

Our base case grows sales about 14% a year with AWS near 40%, lifts net margin by two points and allows a modest de-rating. That earns slightly more than the cost of equity over 12 months. We would turn positive if 2027 capex levelled off while AWS stayed above 40%, and negative if AWS growth fell below 30%.

upside_risks.how: With operating cash flow of $168B and rising, flat capex would swing free cash flow by tens of billions.
Over 40% growth on a $184B run rate would add more profit than the whole retail business earns.
